app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

symptoms.potential_symptom: Proxy-induced request loop causing extreme end-to-end latency
symptoms.evidence: Multiple slow traces (30 total) show extremely high latencies and repeated alternation with frontend. Example traces: cc13cb3f296b74bb985d64b372a1cb15 (latency_ms=301722.464, has_error=true), 6732b07e45a2522a3696254e27fbb252 (242635.858), 23f69b6e2bcbb119d906bf6b30ee5653 (233160.777). Their sequences repeatedly include 'frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog -> frontend-proxy -> frontend' (many cycles), indicating frontend-proxy is forwarding requests back to frontend in a cyclic pattern, producing severe end-to-end latency and errors.

symptoms.potential_symptom: Frontend repeatedly invoking through proxy (cyclic calls) causing request amplification and slow responses
symptoms.evidence: Same slow traces show frontend appearing both as caller and callee in long cyclical sequences (e.g., trace b50a7545e1ff86ecde98f778aab49447 latency_ms=219672.938, trace b388cd7b9139fef8497c1a15cd90e6f9 latency_ms=186495.961). Sequences such as 'frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> cart ...' repeat many times, indicating frontend is involved in a loop with frontend-proxy that amplifies requests and leads to the observed high latencies and has_error=true flags.

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Confirm the proxy-induced loop by examining traces for the repeated sequence (frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog -> frontend-proxy -> ...). Hypothesis: frontend-proxy routing is forwarding requests back to frontend (proxy routing/cluster mapping problem) and is the epicenter of the high-latency cyclical traces.
suggested_tools: get_trace (pick 1 representative high-latency trace e.g. cc13cb3f296b74bb985d64b372a1cb15)

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Two-sided connection/config check between frontend and frontend-proxy to catch misconfigured host/port/service name. Testable hypothesis: frontend's configured upstream URL/host/port (env var or ConfigMap) does not match the frontend-proxy Service definition (name/port/targetPort), causing requests to be routed incorrectly and producing loops.
suggested_tools: kubectl_describe (pod: frontend-559ccb996b-6g85z) -- inspect env vars/args/ConfigMap mounts for upstream/proxy URL
kubectl_describe (service: frontend-proxy) -- inspect ports, service name, selectors and clusterIP

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Validate frontend runtime behavior for outbound calls. Hypothesis: frontend is issuing outbound requests to the proxy (or to a hostname that resolves to the proxy/self), making it both caller and callee and amplifying requests.
suggested_tools: get_logs (pod: frontend-559ccb996b-6g85z) -- search for repeated outbound requests/hostnames/URLs and timestamps matching trace cycles
get_traces (filter: service=frontend, latency>100s) -- confirm frontend appears as both caller and callee in same traces

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Inspect frontend-proxy runtime (Envoy) configuration and logs for incorrect route/cluster mappings. Hypothesis: Envoy/proxy route table or bootstrap config maps backend clusters (product-catalog, etc.) to the frontend service or routes a backend to the proxy itself, causing the observed cycles.
suggested_tools: get_logs (pod(s) backing service: frontend-proxy) -- look for Envoy config dumps, route/cluster assignments, errors
kubectl_describe (pod(s) frontend-proxy) -- inspect args/ConfigMap/volume mounts that provide Envoy bootstrap/config

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Check Service selectors/endpoints for product-catalog and frontend so that product-catalog traffic does not resolve to frontend pods. Hypothesis: product-catalog Service selector or Endpoints are misconfigured and select frontend pods (selector collision), causing requests to be routed back to frontend and creating the loop.
suggested_tools: kubectl_describe (service: product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-jsv8h) -- check selector, ports, Endpoints section
get_pods_from_service (service: product-catalog) -- verify which pods back the product-catalog service (should be product-catalog pods only)

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Take a cluster topology snapshot to surface naming collisions, duplicate services, or port conflicts among frontend, frontend-proxy and the services in data_dependencies. Hypothesis: cluster-level naming/port collisions or duplicate Service objects contribute to misrouting and the proxy loop.
suggested_tools: get_cluster_pods_and_services (namespace: astronomy-shop) -- snapshot services, pods, labels and ports to detect collisions/duplicates

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Confirmed proxy-induced routing loop: requests are cycling between frontend-proxy and frontend because frontend is making HTTP calls to the proxy hostname (http://frontend-proxy:8080/...), and Envoy (frontend-proxy) is routing those requests back to the frontend cluster. This creates repeated frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> ... cycles that cause the high-latency/error traces.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning:
1) get_traces (service=frontend-proxy, errors, high latency) returned many traces whose sequences repeatedly contain "frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend ...", directly showing the cycle.
2) Detailed trace e6ff25a347e5d4ede4591d2f21623aaa shows concrete span evidence: multiple server spans have http.url set to "http://frontend-proxy:8080/…" and frontend server spans list server.address="frontend-proxy" (meaning the frontend is calling the proxy hostname). Envoy client/egress spans show upstream_cluster="frontend" and upstream_address=10.96.21.81:8080 (proxy forwarding to the frontend). One Envoy egress span (spanID c761e6...) is marked canceled/error with a very long duration and upstream_cluster=frontend, and an ingress span shows http.status_code=504 — consistent with requests looping until timeout. Together these unique findings confirm a proxy routing/hostname misconfiguration causing the cyclical proxy-induced loop.

task.investigation_goal: Confirm the proxy-induced loop by examining traces for the repeated sequence (frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog -> frontend-proxy -> ...). Hypothesis: frontend-proxy routing is forwarding requests back to frontend (proxy routing/cluster mapping problem) and is the epicenter of the high-latency cyclical traces.
suggested_tools: get_trace (pick 1 representative high-latency trace e.g. cc13cb3f296b74bb985d64b372a1cb15)

insights: Multiple error traces for frontend-proxy exhibited very high latencies (many ~15s, several >100s up to ~158s) and trace sequences that repeatedly cycled between frontend-proxy and frontend.

Span-level evidence shows the frontend service issued HTTP calls whose URL/hostnames targeted the proxy (http://frontend-proxy:8080/...), and frontend server spans list server.address='frontend-proxy' — i.e., frontend is calling the proxy by name.

Envoy (frontend-proxy) egress/client spans show upstream_cluster='frontend' and upstream_address pointing to port 8080 on the cluster (10.96.21.81:8080), meaning the proxy routes those incoming calls back to the frontend service, completing the cycle.

The loop produced error/cancel conditions: Envoy egress spans with canceled=true and error=true and server spans with http.status_code=504 and response_flags 'UT' (upstream timeout), consistent with requests circulating until timeout.

Root cause (confirmed): a proxy-induced routing loop caused by frontend making requests to the proxy hostname (frontend-proxy), resulting in requests being forwarded back and forth between frontend and frontend-proxy.

Secondary services (product-catalog, cart, checkout, database, redis, quote, shipping, currency, payment) show successful spans and normal responses in the inspected traces, indicating they were not the primary cause of the latency/errors.
Impact: increased latency, timeouts (504), and error traces originating at frontend-proxy due to the cyclical routing behavior rather than downstream service failures.

args.diagnosis: Confirmed proxy-induced routing loop: requests are cycling between frontend-proxy and frontend because frontend is making HTTP calls to the proxy hostname (http://frontend-proxy:8080/...), and Envoy (frontend-proxy) is routing those requests back to the frontend cluster. This creates repeated frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> ... cycles that cause the high-latency/error traces.
args.reasoning:
1) get_traces (service=frontend-proxy, errors, high latency) returned many traces whose sequences repeatedly contain "frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend ...", directly showing the cycle.
2) Detailed trace e6ff25a347e5d4ede4591d2f21623aaa shows concrete span evidence: multiple server spans have http.url set to "http://frontend-proxy:8080/…" and frontend server spans list server.address="frontend-proxy" (meaning the frontend is calling the proxy hostname). Envoy client/egress spans show upstream_cluster="frontend" and upstream_address=10.96.21.81:8080 (proxy forwarding to the frontend). One Envoy egress span (spanID c761e6...) is marked canceled/error with a very long duration and upstream_cluster=frontend, and an ingress span shows http.status_code=504 — consistent with requests looping until timeout. Together these unique findings confirm a proxy routing/hostname misconfiguration causing the cyclical proxy-induced loop.

final_report.root_cause: A proxy-induced routing loop caused by a misconfigured frontend proxy (Envoy) routing table/cluster mapping. Requests from the frontend to the proxy were routed by frontend-proxy back to the frontend upstream cluster (upstream_cluster='frontend' / upstream_address pointing to frontend pod IP:8080), producing repeated frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy cycles that amplified latency and caused timeouts (504) and canceled upstream requests.
affected_resources: message bus (Kafka) and email service (order confirmation) — downstream systems experienced increased latency/timeouts
final_report.evidence_summary: High-latency/error traces (30 total) show cyclical span sequences such as 'frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy -> frontend ...' with extreme end-to-end latencies (examples: trace cc13cb3f296b74bb985d64b372a1cb15 latency_ms=301,722; 6732b07e45a2522a3696254e27fbb252 latency_ms=242,635). Detailed trace inspection (e6ff25a347e5d4ede4591d2f21623aaa and others) shows frontend server spans with http.url referencing 'http://frontend-proxy:8080/…' and server.address='frontend-proxy'. Envoy (frontend-proxy) egress/client spans report upstream_cluster='frontend' and upstream_address pointing to a frontend pod IP (e.g., 10.96.21.81:8080). Envoy egress spans are long and marked canceled/error and ingress server spans show http.status_code=504 with response_flags 'UT' — consistent with requests looping until upstream timeout. Kubernetes inspection shows a frontend pod env var FRONTEND_ADDR set to 'frontend:8080' while the proxy Service is named 'frontend-proxy' (ClusterIP 10.96.199.126:8080) — a naming/configuration mismatch was also observed in pod/service configs.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 trace analysis (completed): retrieved high-latency/error traces for service frontend-proxy and inspected representative traces; observed repeated cycles between frontend-proxy and frontend and span attributes that prove the proxy forwarded requests back to the frontend upstream. Priority-2 configuration check (completed): inspected frontend pod environment and proxy Service; found a mismatch in configured names (FRONTEND_ADDR='frontend:8080' vs proxy Service name 'frontend-proxy:8080') indicating additional configuration inconsistencies. Steps performed: get_traces (frontend-proxy), get_trace (representative high-latency traces), span-level attribute analysis (http.url, server.address, upstream_cluster, upstream_address, response_flags, http.status_code, canceled/error), kubectl_describe of frontend pod and frontend-proxy Service. Conclusion: request loop originates at frontend-proxy routing requests back to frontend, producing amplification and timeouts. While frontend configuration shows inconsistent naming which may have contributed to confusion, the proximate cause of the loop is the proxy's incorrect routing/cluster mapping.
